And the way P=NP is sold to the public is that it is believed that P=NP is true. Worded in the same positive sense as the Riemann hypothesis, when in fact it is the complete opposite. >IF P=NP, why would it matter
Because the proof will take the form of demonstrating how to solve an NP problem in polynomial time. And one of the fun aspects of NP is that *all* NP problems are all minor variants of the same underlying problem - you can convert any NP problem into any other NP problem in polynomial time, and doing so is part of the proof that a problem is in NP. So if a polynomial time solution is found for *any* NP problem, then *all* NP problems are suddenly solvable in polynomial time, because you can take your pet problem, convert it to the now-known-P problem (in polynomial time) solve it there (using the newly discovered polynomial time algorithm) and convert that result back to your original problem (in polynomial time).
